passage: "Open-air quiz on the terrace, four o'clock, in May," said Mehak. "Done?" "Done!" said Ritesh at once. "Sounds great," said Pia. "Fine with me," said Karan. Hansa, holding the pen, looked at the sun burning on the window. It will be very hot at four, she thought. "Hansa? Minutes?" "Yes. Open-air, four o'clock, May." She wrote it down. "Perfect," said Mehak. "Meeting over." Ritesh grabbed his bag. In the corridor Hansa whispered to Pia, "Do you think the terrace will be too hot?" "I was thinking the same," said Pia, "but nobody said."

qa.q: What time and month did Mehak propose for the quiz?
qa.a: Mehak proposed a quiz on the terrace at four o'clock in May.

qa.q: Why did Hansa write down the plan without mentioning the heat?
qa.a: Hansa did not want to spoil the mood or be the only doubter, so the worry stayed inside; the whisper in the corridor shows the doubt was real.

qa.q: What could the committee do differently at the moment Mehak says "Done?"
qa.a: Someone could ask "Does anyone see a problem?" or set a short pause, so doubts like the heat can be raised before the plan is fixed.

qa.q: What might it be like for Pia, who had the same doubt but said "Sounds great"?
qa.a: Pia probably feels a little regretful and relieved on finding Hansa thought the same; the quick agreement hid a doubt that two people held.

grounding: A group of teens planning an event rushes to agree with the loudest member, and doubts stay unspoken so a poor plan goes ahead.

passage: I am Pooja, and I was on the cultural committee in Class 11. Dilnaz loves big ideas, and at the meeting she said, "Let us do forty stalls and a stage show on the same day." Everyone clapped. I was thinking about volunteers, because we barely had twelve. But the room was happy, Dilnaz was glowing, and I did not want to be the one who said no. So I said, "Great idea." Three others told me later that they had been worried too. Five days before the fete we still had no volunteers, and half the stalls were empty tables. Dilnaz looked at me and asked, "Why did nobody say anything?" I had no answer.

qa.q: How many volunteers did the committee barely have?
qa.a: The committee barely had twelve volunteers.

qa.q: Why did Pooja say "Great idea" while thinking about volunteers?
qa.a: Pooja did not want to be the one who spoiled the happy mood, so a real worry stayed unspoken; the feeling was a wish to keep the peace.

qa.q: What might Pooja have done at the meeting to raise the concern without spoiling the mood?
qa.a: Pooja could have said "I love it, can we check how many volunteers we need?", turning the doubt into a practical question.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz feel when asking "Why did nobody say anything?"
qa.a: Dilnaz may feel surprised and a bit hurt, having believed everyone shared the excitement; the question suggests Dilnaz wants honest views next time.

grounding: A group of teens rushes to agree with the loudest member, doubts stay unspoken and a poor plan goes ahead.

passage:
The farewell committee met in the empty Class 11 room of the government school at Kurukshetra. Wasim sat on the teacher's desk, swinging his legs.
“Riverbank. Evening. Bonfire, music, the whole thing,” he announced. “Last week of June.”
“Wow!” said Sukhi. “Yes!” said Dinesh. Everyone clapped.
Indu opened her mouth. Last June the river had flooded the path. Also, half the girls' parents would never allow an evening by the river. She looked at the smiling faces and closed her mouth. Nobody wanted to ruin it.
“All agreed?” Wasim asked. Every hand went up. Hers too.
On the day, it rained from noon. The farewell was cancelled at five, and they had no other plan.

qa.q: When did Wasim want the farewell?
qa.a: He wanted it in the last week of June.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling when she closed her mouth?
qa.a: She felt doubtful and uneasy about the plan, but didn't want to spoil everyone's excitement.

qa.q: What small step could have helped the committee?
qa.a: Someone could ask, "What could go wrong?" before voting, so Indu's worries about rain and parents came out.

qa.q: How might Wasim see the cancellation?
qa.a: He might feel disappointed and embarrassed, perhaps wishing someone had raised the risk of rain before.

grounding: Shows a teen committee rushing to agree with its loudest member while a doubter stays silent, so a poor plan goes ahead.

passage:
The student council at Gabriel's school in Lisbon had twenty minutes to plan the charity bake sale.
Nadia spoke first and loudest. “Last day before the holidays. Everyone's happy, they'll buy loads!”
“Perfect,” said Tiago. “Love it,” said Beatriz.
Gabriel frowned at his notebook. Half the school left early that day for trips. But everyone was grinning, and Nadia was already drawing a poster. He didn't want to be the one who killed the mood.
“Any objections?” asked the teacher.
Silence. Gabriel shook his head.
On the day, the canteen was nearly empty. They sold a third of the cakes. Afterwards Beatriz muttered, “I knew half the school would be gone.” Gabriel stared at her.

qa.q: What did Beatriz mutter afterwards?
qa.a: She muttered, "I knew half the school would be gone."

qa.q: What was Gabriel feeling when he shook his head?
qa.a: He felt doubtful and hesitant, but was afraid of being the one who killed the mood.

qa.q: What would you advise the council for their next event?
qa.a: Before agreeing, each member could name one risk, so doubts like Gabriel's and Beatriz's are heard early.

qa.q: How might Nadia feel if she learned others had doubts?
qa.a: Nadia might feel surprised and a bit hurt that nobody spoke up, since Nadia was only excited, not trying to silence anyone.

grounding: Shows a teen council rushing to agree with its loudest member while doubts stay unspoken, so a poor plan goes ahead.

passage:
The hostel mess committee met after dinner in the warden's office. Diwali night was the only item.
Asif, the mess secretary, was already standing. “DJ on the terrace, eight till two. Full volume. Best night of the year!”
The others cheered. “Asif bhai zindabad!”
Manoj sat at the end of the bench. Their physics exam was on the morning after Diwali. And the warden had said the terrace railing was loose. He glanced around. Everyone looked so happy.
“Anyone against?” Asif asked, grinning.
Manoj looked down.
“Passed!”
On Diwali night the warden stopped the music at ten because of the railing. Next morning, half the hostel dragged into the exam hall with red eyes.

qa.q: Where did the committee meet?
qa.a: They met in the warden's office after dinner.

qa.q: What was Manoj feeling when Asif asked "Anyone against?"
qa.a: He felt doubtful and worried about the exam and the loose railing, but too hesitant to spoil the cheering.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could have fixed it?
qa.a: Everyone agreed too quickly with Asif; if Manoj had raised the exam and the railing, the plan could have been changed early.

qa.q: How might the warden see the committee's plan?
qa.a: The warden probably felt frustrated, having to stop the music for safety because the committee hadn't thought about the loose railing.

grounding: Shows a hostel committee rushing to agree with its loudest member while doubts about exams and safety stay unspoken.

passage:
Dear Nilesh bhaiya,
You asked how the Class 12 farewell went. Short version: it rained, and I saw it coming.
At the committee meeting, Aarav stood up and said, "Open-air DJ night on the terrace, fairy lights, done." Everyone clapped. I was thinking: it's July, and the terrace has no roof. Sneha caught my eye like she was thinking the same thing. Neither of us said it. Riya said "Perfect!" and the vote was over in two minutes. Nobody wanted to be the one who spoiled the mood.
On the day, it poured at seven. We dragged the speakers into the chemistry corridor and the seniors stood around in wet shoes. Afterwards Sneha told me she'd wanted to suggest the auditorium. So had I.
Next time I'm going to say the boring thing out loud.
Jyoti

qa.q: Which month was the farewell planned in?
qa.a: It was July.

qa.q: Why did Jyoti keep the doubt about the terrace quiet?
qa.a: Jyoti felt nervous about spoiling the happy, clapping mood and going against Aarav's confident plan.

qa.q: What small step could the committee try before voting next time?
qa.a: Pause for a minute and let each member name one thing that could go wrong before anyone claps a plan through.

qa.q: How might Sneha feel on hearing Jyoti had the same doubt?
qa.a: Sneha may feel frustrated that two silent people could have changed the plan, and a little relieved not to have been alone.

grounding: Illustrates a teen committee rushing to agree with the loudest member while doubts stay unspoken and a poor plan goes ahead.
